بَاقلٌ : see بَقِلٌ. ―
-b2- Also, as an epithet applied to the [tree, or shrub, called] رِمْث, (S, K,) Becoming green: (K:) or putting forth what resemble young wingless locusts, and showing the greenness of its leaves: they did not say ↓ مُبْقِلٌ [in this sense], in like manner as [it is commonly asserted that] they did not say مُورِسٌ, from أَوْرَسَ, but وَاِرسٌ. (S.) ―
-b3- Also What comes forth, or come forth, in the sides of trees, in the days of the رَبِيع [or spring], before their leaves become apparent. (JK.) [See 4.]
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
